items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, though claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can close the door on your case entirely.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be All-or-Nothing
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the crash. Your compensation is simply reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages, such as pain and suffering, in ordinary injury cases. That means your claim isn't artificially limited before it's even evaluated.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you recover compensation. That lets you focus on healing instead of worrying about legal bills.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in California?
items.answer: In most cases, you have two years from the date of the injury to file a lawsuit. If your claim involves a government entity, such as a city-maintained road, the deadline to file a notice can be as short as six months, so it's wise not to delay.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame. Your total recovery is reduced by your percentage of fault, but it isn't barred outright.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen in Palos Verdes Estates?
items.answer: Public collision records show that corridors including Palos Verdes Drive W, Via Del Monte, Palos Verdes Drive West, and Granvia Altamira have the highest recorded counts of injury collisions in recent data. These are simply public-record figures, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: No. California does not cap non-economic damages, like pain and suffering, in standard personal injury cases. This is different from some other states that impose such limits.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No, connecting with an attorney through LawProactive is completely free, and LawProactive itself is not a law firm. If you choose to move forward, attorneys in the network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation.
